source.title: Tracking multiple independent targets: Evidence for a parallel tracking mechanism.

confidence_rationale: The foundational multiple-object-tracking demonstration: observers track ~4-5 target items among identical moving distractors, which Pylyshyn explains with FINST visual indexes -- a small set of pre-conceptual pointers that INDIVIDUATE and stick to objects across motion without encoding their features or locations. This grounds two ARC-006 properties at once: entities are SPARSE (a hard ~4-5 index limit) and PERSISTENT/bindable (the index sticks to the same token through motion). It also grounds the token-instance individuation MECH-045 needs. Held mid-band because the items are featureless identical dots (it isolates individuation/tracking but says nothing about feature BINDING per se), the capacity limit is debated, and it is human psychophysics.
failure_signatures: The tracked items are identical featureless dots, so the paradigm isolates pure INDIVIDUATION+tracking and is silent on feature binding -- it cannot ground ARC-006's bindable-feature-bundle clause, only its sparse-persistent-token clause.

The ~4-5 index capacity is a strong, debated empirical limit; a REE that hard-codes a small fixed slot count would inherit a specific psychophysical number whose generality (and dependence on speed/spacing) is contested.

FINST indexes are pre-conceptual location-trackers that explicitly do NOT carry identity/feature content; treating them as full object files over-reads the construct -- indexing is necessary for, but distinct from, the object-file buffer.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Observers can track up to ~4-5 independently and unpredictably moving target items among identical distractors far better than a serial location-updating algorithm predicts, implying a parallel pre-attentive mechanism (FINST indexes) that individuates a small number of objects and maintains their identity across motion without encoding their features or trajectories.
mapping.ree_translation: ARC-006 says entities are 'sparse, persistent, bindable structures'. Pylyshyn & Storm supplies direct evidence for the SPARSE (a hard small-number index limit) and PERSISTENT (the same token tracked through motion) properties, via a mechanism -- visual indexing -- that individuates objects before any feature/identity is bound. For MECH-045 it grounds the prior step the object-file buffer depends on: you must first individuate and stick a pointer to a token before you can persist its features.
mapping.mapping_caveat: FINST indexes track featureless tokens and carry NO feature/identity content, so this grounds individuation and persistence-of-pointer, not feature binding or the contents of an object file. The ~4-5 capacity is a contested empirical number REE should not hard-code as a fixed slot count. Human psychophysics to latent-stack agent transfer applies.
mapping.source_context: Human visual psychophysics; tracking 4-5 of 10 identical randomly-moving dots and detecting a target-vs-distractor change.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational MOT/FINST study. Mapping good for the sparse+persistent-token clauses of ARC-006; discounted because featureless dots isolate individuation and say nothing about feature binding, and the capacity number is debated.
